description: Ingeniería, datos y software inteligente para la próxima frontera espacial.
summary: Star Helpy is an intelligent early-warning web application designed to protect the mental and physical health of astronauts on long-duration missions, such as trips to Mars. Due to communication delays with Earth, the platform runs 100% locally on low-cost hardware without relying on the internet. Through daily check-ins taking under a minute, an interactive body map, and biometric tracking based on the crew member's personal baseline, it detects fatigue, stress, and cognitive decline early, adapting exercise and wellness routines according to their spatial location to ensure mission safety.
details:
• The Problem and Space Hazards
    Long-duration space missions to Mars face five critical hazards for the crew: radiation, isolation, distance, altered gravity, and a hostile environment. On such distant journeys, there is no possibility of rapid evacuation or immediate medical assistance on Earth, compounded by communication delays of up to 20 minutes each way. The biomedical and environmental indicators measured by the project stem directly from these risk factors.
  • The Solution: What is Star Helpy and how does it work?
    Star Helpy is an intelligent early-warning and wellness web application designed to help astronauts care for themselves autonomously. In under 60 seconds, the interface displays a status traffic light, key heart rate metrics, environmental radiation, and elapsed mission days. Additionally, it includes an interactive body map to report physical discomfort and a local conversational assistant that guides the crew member in real time.
  • Differentiating Factors and Innovation
    The system stands out through three fundamental pillars: it uses a personal baseline to compare the astronaut against themselves before the trip (rather than general averages), adapts its recommendations based on the mission location (space station, the Moon, or Mars), and features a quality control system that warns if a measurement is missing to prevent false senses of security.
  • Scientific Foundations and Technologies Used
    For its development, the team relied on the five hazards of NASA's Human Research Program (NASA HRP) and data from space APIs such as OSDR, RadLab, and EDA / NASA DONKI. Technologically, the system uses Python for data processing, Angular for the user interface, and Oracle for database management.
  • Viability and Sustainability
    The project is highly viable because it operates locally without relying on onboard internet, running on low-power, affordable hardware (such as a Raspberry Pi 5 or an Nvidia Jetson Orin Nano). It is aimed as a commercial and R&D solution for private spaceflight companies and space agencies interested in reducing crew stress efficiently and cost-effectively.
